C0.quote: committee of experts to vote on a multi-attribute alternative
C0.note: Strategic voting in committees under k-majority rules; equilibrium voting analysis.

C1.quote: we solve for symmetric (Bayesian-Nash) equilibria of the voting game
C1.note: Equilibrium voting characterised; principal's payoff compared for committee composition (welfare-like objective of principal). No axioms, simulations, or data.

C2.2.note: Binary Yes/No votes on a single alternative vs status quo; this is not rankings, approval sets, or cardinal reports.

C2.3.quote: expert i may also value others’ signals about the alternative
C2.3.note: Interdependent payoffs v_i^A, private signals are held attitudes.

C2.4.quote: Expert i is said to vote sincerely if he conditions his vote only
C2.4.note: Votes (cutoff strategies) are separate from signals and payoffs; strategic voting differs from sincere.

C3.1.quote: equilibrium voting is generically strategic and depends on the degree of partisanship
C3.1.note: Experts vote strategically in equilibrium; the uninformed follow best responses too. The principal's optimal-voting benchmark is not strategic dictation, but all voters are equilibrium players, so arguably ALL; benchmark analysis is not about voters misreporting. Choose SOME because the optimal-voting benchmark dictates cutoffs.

C3.2.quote: Suppose that the principal could dictate the cutoff x
C3.2.note: In the benchmark, the principal dictates cutoffs; voters are not modelled as strategic. Sincerity is not stated for this benchmark, and sincere voting is only a special equilibrium case. This is borderline; coded NOT-STATED would also fit.

C3.3.quote: Suppose that the principal could dictate the cutoff x
C3.3.note: No reason for sincerity is given for the benchmark.

C4.1.note: Input is Yes/No vote (OTH), not RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR.

C5.1.quote: the principal who cares about the alternative’s average quality
C5.1.note: Principal's payoff, i.e. average quality (utilitarian welfare, footnote 9), is evaluated for committee composition.

C5.2.quote: The principal, representing the organization, cares about the average quality
C5.2.note: Evaluated on signals θ_i, which are held and defined separately from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: we solve for symmetric (Bayesian-Nash) equilibria of the voting game
VOT.quote_info: each expert receives private information about the “quality” of one attribute
VOT.note: Each knows own signal and the distribution F; conditions on pivotal event.

ORG.quote_behav: the principal may try to influence the equilibrium voting by appointing
ORG.quote_info: An uninformed principal must decide between the status quo
ORG.note: Principal chooses committee composition β, information λ, and size; she is the committee appointer (organiser). Uninformed about signals.

C7.1.note: Both voters and principal are STRAT.

C8.1.quote: we solve for symmetric (Bayesian-Nash) equilibria of the voting game
C8.1.note: The principal's choice is an optimisation over β given equilibrium, a Stackelberg-like structure; not coded separately.
